title: Wave 6a: Plan and sequences
summary: Wave 6a of web/spec/README.md section 7 at integration: the Plan screen (Steps table editors, issues never clamped, Source with exoplanet transits, Run options, Presets and Save, Target set, VisibilityTimeline), the run (transport with Start at a time, readiness chip and Preflight, run strip, Run card in Observe, the status bar's one progress item), the mount-motion interlock and the palette's run entries, against the headless server in simulator replay mode on copies of real RR Lyr raw frames (2026-09-25; Settings site replaced by public Paris coordinates; check star 000-BJW-666 assigned on the copies). A run started, paused, resumed and stopped through the UI gave 19 subs whose 133 points (2 527 values) equal the fixed Qt sequence path's with no difference; observation.json of a transit plan written through the UI is byte-identical to Qt's (progress.md, Wave 6a). Captured at device scale 2: 15 scenes in the three themes at 1 440 x 900 and in Observatory at 1 280 x 800, plus the palette; scenes 01-12 were re-captured and 14-16 added by the wave 6a fixer after the design, technical and science reviews (the palette is the integrator's). The 15 Night Red originals pass the audit (rules A and B, 0 px each).

A variable-star plan (fixer re-capture): RR Lyr found in the Source card; Steps sized to their content, so the Visibility timeline takes the rest of the column. The timeline header has two rows: the facts (site, night, 'highest at night 65.9° at 18:03 (dusk)': RR Lyr culminates before dusk, so it is not called a peak) and, on its own row, the run check, never cut. The 'planned run', 'now' and night-high labels carry a thin halo instead of a filled box, so the altitude curve stays visible under them. Totals end time in UTC ('ends ≈ … UTC', local time in the tooltip). Gain grouped like every number. Target set with the check star 000-BJW-666 assigned on the copies; Start is the one brass action. (observatory, 1440x900, device scale 2.)

An exoplanet transit written through the UI (fixer re-capture; the earlier Observatory 1440 shot had a stale coverage): HD 189733 b, night 2027-07-31, baseline 45 min each side. The card puts UTC first ('21:52 → 01:11 UTC · 3.32 h', local below), names the altitudes ('start 59° · mid 64° · end 55°') and separates the title ('HD 189733 b · host HD 189733'). The plan notes read 'Transit sequence prepared: 921 light frames at a 13.0 s cadence.' and 'Starts at the coverage start, 2027-07-31 21:52 UTC.' (no raw ISO time). The timeline's run verdict is on its own row ('starts 5m 54s before astronomical dusk'); the coverage band and the planned run come from the same prediction; the transit label has a halo over the hatch. The chip reads 'Blocked · start time and 1 more' (more than 24 h ahead; the disk). (observatory, 1440x900, device scale 2.)

The mount-motion interlock (fixer re-capture, design review high finding): GoTo from the Mount card during a run. The dialog says what the command would do ('GoTo would move the field under the run. Pausing lets the 10 s sub in progress finish and be saved; the mount then moves, and the run stays paused until you resume it.'), the safe answer is 'Keep running' (as in the Stop dialog, focused), and the way through is a hold-to-confirm control (BRAND 7: icon and label at 40 px, secondary, no brass fill; 'Hold 0.7 s to pause the run and slew · Enter to confirm'). The client now waits as long as the server may hold the request (sub in progress + 75 s, 400 s in autofocus). (observatory, 1440x900, device scale 2.)
